title: Operational Works Scheduler
description:
Operational Works Scheduler

Connect 2 Swindon are recruiting an Operational Works Scheduler, to support Swindon Council on a temporary contract until February 2027.

Job Role
- To manage the day-to-day planning across all operations by ensuring jobs are adequately allocated, attended, re-booked, or forwarded as necessary.
- To monitor scheduling systems ensuring appointments made are kept by the workforce and report appointment failings immediately to the senior planner/operational supervisors.
- To work within a multi-skilled approach using appropriate IT systems to best match the needs of different operational services.
- Act as the first point of contact for Operational teams by answering phone calls via the dedicated scheduling line and supporting customer service calls when required.
- Plan work for pre - and post-inspections, reactive and scheduled repairs, and deliveries across all operational services, prioritising emergency jobs as necessary, potentially managing up to 30 operatives.
- Ensure all work orders are scheduled upon agreed service level agreements (SLAs) and completed within target timescales to meet key performance indicators (KPIs).
- Contact customers to keep them informed of any changes to agreed appointments.

Key Accountability's
- Update and maintain operative diaries with availability, including sickness, holidays, and training, using Dynamic Resource Scheduler (or equivalent).
- Action Dynamic Scheduler lists daily, ensuring further works, missed appointments, materials requirements, and trades bookings are handled within KPI timescales.
- Operate in accordance with statutory guidance to meet operational servicing targets.
- Maintain acceptable levels of work-in-progress and backlog.
- Identify staffing or operational concerns and communicate promptly with the Operational Manager.
- Contact tenants as necessary to inform them of appointment changes.
- Maintain a positive attitude on calls without offering technical advice; refer technical matters to the Operations Manager.
- Demonstrate excellent telephone skills, including the ability to deal with irate or challenging customers calmly and professionally.
- Utilise strong problem-solving skills to resolve issues before escalation to the Operations Manager.
- Handle sensitive information with discretion.
- Employ effective negotiation skills across public, operational managers, and contractors.

Supplementary Accountability's
- Undertake any other duties consistent with the post's grading and specialist qualifications.
- Adhere to Health & Safety requirements as outlined in the Health & Safety at Work Act 1974 and Management of Health & Safety at Work Regulations 1999.
- Cooperate with the Council to ensure compliance with statutory health and safety duties.
- Work according to training/instructions, use PPE properly, and report any hazards or risks.
- Fulfil responsibilities outlined in the Directorate Health and Safety Policy.

Knowledge & Experience
- Proficient with Word, Excel, Outlook.
- Experienced with Dynamic Resource Scheduler or equivalent scheduling software.
- Familiarity with databases and data management.

Qualifications

Educated to GCSE Level in English and Maths, Grade A to C or equivalent.

Decision Making
- Ability to make effective decisions quickly, demonstrating initiative in problem resolution.
- Achievements through both teamwork and individual effort.

Creativity and Innovation
- Resourceful in delivering service efficiently.
- Demonstrates innovation through teamwork and individual contributions.

Additional Responsibilities
- Collaborate closely with teams to finalise schedules.
- Monitor progress against project milestones.
- Proactively manage scheduling conflicts and communicate changes swiftly.
- Generate reports and visualise operational health using software tools.
- Engage in continuous learning to improve planning methodologies and adopt emerging technologies.

We encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply. Join us in building a workplace that empowers every individual to succeed.

Commercial Services Trading Ltd is acting as an Employment Business in relation to this vacancy.

title: Inbound Banking Customer Service Advisors
description:

A genuine passion for doing the right thing for customers.
Comfort using desktop or laptop computers, with access to a secure and reliable internet connection.
Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment while maintaining excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
Confidence on the phone and the ability to build rapport with members.

Why Apply?

This opportunity not only offers a competitive hourly rate and a supportive work environment but also the chance to be part of an organisation that values its members and strives to reflect their diversity. Experience in financial services is not necessary, as comprehensive training will be provided.

If you are ready to embrace a new challenge and contribute positively to customer experiences, consider applying today!

Scanning of patient related documentation and attaching scanned documents to patients healthcare records r. Process requests for information i.e. SAR, insurance / solicitors letters and DVLA forms to the administrative team s. title: GP Receptionist
description: The purpose of the Receptionist role is to provide a high-quality, professional reception and administrative service to patients, doctors, staff, colleagues, and other healthcare professionals, portraying the Practice in the highest possible professional manner. Receptionists are responsible for ensuring patients can access the healthcare services they need efficiently and courteously. They play a key role in supporting the day-to-day running of the practice and in ensuring the smooth flow of communication between patients and staff. Flexibility is essential for this role, and you will be required to provide additional cover during staff holidays or sickness. - Ensure an effective and efficient reception service is provided to patients and any other visitors to the practice. - Deal with all general enquiries, explain procedures and make new and follow-up appointments. - Use your own judgment and communication skills. - Explain practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover, and ensure procedures are completed. - Receive and make telephone calls as required. Divert calls and take messages, ensuring accuracy of detail and prompt appropriate delivery. - Enter requests for home visits into the clinical system, ensuring to carefully record all relevant details and referring to the rota doctor where necessary. - Enter patient information on to the computer as required. - Open and distribute incoming mail. - Photocopy and shred documentation. - Open up premises at the start of the day when first to arrive, de-activate alarm and make all necessary preparations to receive patients. - When last to leave at the end of the day, ensure that the building is totally secured, internal lights are off and the alarm activated. - Keep the reception area, noticeboards and leaflet dispensers tidy and free from obstructions and clutter. - Assist with the induction of new reception staff. - Support reception team members in managing busy periods and resolving patient queries effectively. - Process new patient registrations and action patient deductions. - Any other delegated duties considered appropriate to the post.
